The circuit also incorporates a primary network of control lines linked to the memory cell array. These lines enable access to any given memory cell's stored data, achieved by sending control signals through a specific pairing (or combination) of at least two lines from this primary network.

# Programmable Memory Element Circuit Architecture

## Overview of Memory Element Array

The circuit architecture centers on an array of programmable memory elements that are fabricated directly onto a substrate. Each individual memory element within this array is constructed with one or more processable regions—physical areas specifically designed to be modified during a programming operation. These processable regions serve as the fundamental building blocks that determine the informational state stored within each memory element.

## Programming Mechanism

The programming of these memory elements is accomplished through an external process in which material is selectively applied to partially cover the processable regions. This material application process is the key mechanism by which each memory element is configured into one of several possible states. By controlling the extent, pattern, or location of material coverage on the processable regions, the circuit fabrication process can effectively encode distinct data values into each memory element, allowing the array to store meaningful information based on the physical configuration established during manufacturing.

## First Control Line Set and Access Mechanism

To enable retrieval of the programmed information, a first set of control lines is electrically connected to the memory element array. This connection scheme is designed such that the content of any individual memory element can be accessed by applying appropriate control signals to specific combinations of at least two control lines from this first set. This multi-line addressing approach allows for selective and precise access to individual elements within the array, ensuring that each memory element's programmed state can be independently read or verified without interference from adjacent elements.

## Second Circuit Element Array

In addition to the memory element array, the overall circuit incorporates a separate array of second circuit elements. These elements are structurally and functionally distinct from the programmable memory elements described above. Each second circuit element is connected to two control lines: one control line selected from the first set (the same set used to access the memory elements) and one control line selected from a second, separate set of control lines dedicated to this purpose.

## Dual Connectivity and Access Provision

This arrangement, wherein each second circuit element maintains connections to both the first and second control line sets, establishes a dedicated addressing mechanism for these elements. The dual connectivity ensures that individual second circuit elements can be selectively identified and accessed within their array, analogous to the selective access scheme employed for the memory elements, but utilizing a combination of control lines drawn from two distinct sets rather than exclusively from the first set alone. This design allows the overall circuit to integrate both memory storage functionality and additional circuit element functionality within a unified control line infrastructure, while maintaining independent and selective access to each type of component.

# Programmable Memory System with Enhanced Selective Access Architecture

## Overview

The circuit described herein presents a sophisticated approach to programmable memory design, addressing longstanding challenges in memory array architecture through a novel combination of selective material processing and dual-access control mechanisms. This design philosophy enables both efficient memory state configuration and expanded functional capability within a single integrated system.

## Core Memory Array Structure

At the heart of this architecture lies an array of memory elements, each incorporating a processable region designed specifically to interact with external processing steps during manufacturing. These processable regions serve as the mechanism by which each individual memory element can be configured to represent one of multiple possible states. This is accomplished through selective coverage of the processable region with a specific material during the fabrication or post-fabrication processing stage.

The selective application of material—which may involve techniques such as selective deposition, masking, or other targeted processing methods—allows manufacturers or programming systems to determine, on an element-by-element basis, which state each memory cell will ultimately hold. This provides significant flexibility in configuring the memory array according to specific application requirements, whether during initial manufacturing or through subsequent programming operations.

Access to these individually configured memory elements is achieved through combinations of control lines drawn from a first set of control lines. This arrangement means that each memory element is not necessarily tied to a single dedicated control line but rather can be addressed through particular combinations of signals across multiple lines within this first set. Such a combinatorial addressing scheme allows for efficient use of control line resources, as a relatively limited number of physical control lines can address a substantially larger number of individual memory elements through various logical combinations.

## Enhanced Architecture: Second Circuit Element Array

Building upon this foundational memory array structure, the design incorporates a significant architectural enhancement: an additional array of second circuit elements. These elements are explicitly distinct from the memory elements described above, serving a different functional purpose within the overall circuit design.

Each of these second circuit elements maintains connections to lines drawn from both control line sets—the first set (shared with the memory element array) and a second, separate set of control lines introduced specifically for this enhanced array. This dual connectivity represents a key innovation in the overall architecture, as it establishes a bridge between the two control line sets while maintaining functional separation between the memory elements and the second circuit elements.

## Functional Benefits of the Dual-Array Approach

The integration of this second array of circuit elements, with its unique dual-line connectivity, provides several important functional advantages:

**Independent Access Capability**: By connecting to both the first and second control line sets, the second circuit elements can be accessed independently of the memory elements. This independence means that operations performed on or through the second circuit elements do not necessarily interfere with or depend upon the state or configuration of the memory array, allowing for more flexible and reliable circuit operation.

**Expanded Functional Versatility**: The presence of this additional array significantly broadens the range of functions the overall circuit can perform. Rather than being limited solely to memory storage and retrieval operations, the circuit can leverage the second circuit elements to implement additional logic, control, verification, or other specialized functions that complement the core memory functionality.

**Efficient Resource Utilization**: By sharing the first set of control lines between both the memory element array and the second circuit element array, the design achieves a degree of efficiency in control line usage. This shared resource approach means that the addition of new functional capability does not require a completely separate and parallel control infrastructure, but rather builds upon and extends the existing control line resources already present for the memory array.

**Scalable Design Framework**: This architecture provides a scalable framework wherein additional functional elements can be incorporated into the overall circuit design without fundamentally restructuring the existing memory array or its associated first control line set. The second control line set can be tailored to the specific requirements of the second circuit elements, providing design flexibility while maintaining compatibility with the established memory architecture.

## Conclusion

This programmable memory system architecture represents a thoughtful integration of selective material processing techniques for memory state configuration with an enhanced dual-array structure that incorporates independently accessible circuit elements. By combining these approaches, the design achieves both the fundamental goal of reliable, configurable memory storage and the expanded goal of increased circuit functionality and versatility, all while maintaining efficient use of control line resources through strategic sharing between the two distinct arrays of circuit elements.

# Circuit Description

A circuit comprises several fundamental components that work together to perform a specific electrical function. In its most basic configuration, a circuit comprises a power source, conductive pathways, and one or more electrical components that either consume, transform, or regulate the flow of current.

## Basic Structure

At the core, a circuit comprises the following essential elements:

- **Power Source**: A battery, power supply, or other source of electrical energy that provides the voltage and current necessary to drive the circuit.
- **Conductors**: Wires or traces that create pathways for electrical current to flow between components.
- **Load Components**: Resistors, capacitors, inductors, transistors, or other elements that perform the intended function of the circuit, whether it be resistance, energy storage, signal amplification, or switching.
- **Control Elements**: Switches, relays, or semiconductor devices that regulate when and how current flows through the circuit.

## Example Implementation

Consider a simple LED indicator circuit. This circuit comprises a DC power source, a current-limiting resistor connected in series with a light-emitting diode, and two terminals for connection to the power supply. When voltage is applied across the terminals, current flows through the resistor, which limits the current to a safe level, and then through the LED, causing it to illuminate.

## More Complex Applications

In more sophisticated systems, a circuit comprises additional elements such as:

1. **Integrated circuits (ICs)** that consolidate multiple functions into a single chip
2. **Feedback loops** that allow the circuit to self-regulate based on output conditions
3. **Filtering components** that remove unwanted noise or frequencies from a signal
4. **Protection circuitry**, such as fuses or diodes, to prevent damage from voltage spikes or reverse current

## Conclusion

Whether simple or complex, every circuit comprises a deliberate arrangement of components designed to achieve a specific electrical outcome. Understanding this fundamental structure—power source, conductive pathway, and functional components—provides the foundation for analyzing and designing electrical and electronic systems across countless applications, from basic household devices to advanced computing systems.

## Claim 1

A programmable memory array comprising:

a substrate having a plurality of memory cells arranged in a matrix of rows and columns;

a plurality of first control lines extending in a first direction across the substrate, each first control line being electrically coupled to a corresponding row of the plurality of memory cells;

a plurality of second control lines extending in a second direction across the substrate, the second direction being transverse to the first direction, each second control line being electrically coupled to a corresponding column of the plurality of memory cells;

wherein each memory cell of the plurality of memory cells comprises a programmable resistive element formed by a physical material deposition process configured to selectively deposit a conductive material between a first electrode and a second electrode of the memory cell, the presence or absence of the deposited conductive material, or a thickness thereof, defining a resistive memory state of the memory cell;

a secondary array of circuit elements disposed in electrical communication with the plurality of memory cells, the secondary array comprising a plurality of selector devices, each selector device being coupled between a respective memory cell and at least one of the first control lines or the second control lines, the selector devices configured to isolate unselected memory cells during a read or write operation; and

a control circuit coupled to the plurality of first control lines and the plurality of second control lines, the control circuit configured to selectively apply a voltage or current bias to a selected first control line and a selected second control line to initiate the physical material deposition process at an intersecting memory cell, thereby programmably setting the resistive memory state of the intersecting memory cell.

## Claim 2 (Dependent)

The programmable memory array of claim 1, wherein the physical material deposition process comprises an electrochemical metallization process configured to grow a conductive filament comprising a metal ion species migrated from the first electrode through an electrolyte layer toward the second electrode in response to the applied voltage or current bias.

## Claim 3 (Dependent)

The programmable memory array of claim 1, wherein each selector device of the secondary array of circuit elements comprises a transistor, a diode, or a threshold switching element.

## Claim 4 (Dependent)

The programmable memory array of claim 1, wherein the control circuit is further configured to apply a reverse voltage or current bias to the selected first control line and the selected second control line to at least partially reverse the physical material deposition process, thereby resetting the resistive memory state of the intersecting memory cell.

The programmable memory array of claim 1, wherein the resistive memory state of each memory cell corresponds to one of at least two discrete resistance levels, each discrete resistance level representing a stored digital value.

## Claim 6 (Dependent)

## Claim 7 (Dependent)

The programmable memory array of claim 1, further comprising a sense circuit coupled to the plurality of second control lines, the sense circuit configured to measure a resistance of a selected memory cell to determine the resistive memory state stored therein.

The programmable memory array of claim 1, wherein the secondary array of circuit elements is disposed on a layer of the substrate different from a layer on which the plurality of memory cells is disposed, the secondary array of circuit elements and the plurality of memory cells being electrically interconnected by a plurality of vertical interconnect structures.

# UNITED STATES PATENT APPLICATION

## MASK-PROGRAMMABLE MEMORY ARRAY WITH SHARED ADDRESSING FOR AUXILIARY NON-MEMORY ELEMENTS

---

### FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to integrated circuit memory devices, and more particularly to a mask-programmable memory architecture in which a plurality of memory cells and a plurality of non-memory circuit elements are commonly addressed via a shared set of row and column control lines, thereby enabling efficient utilization of decoder and addressing infrastructure across heterogeneous circuit elements disposed within a common array region of a semiconductor substrate.

---

### BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Mask-programmable read-only memory (MPROM) devices are well known in the art, wherein the logical state of each memory cell is determined during fabrication through selective inclusion or omission of a conductive via, contact, or diffusion implant at a predetermined mask layer, rather than through post-fabrication electrical programming. Such devices typically comprise an array of memory cells organized into rows and columns, each cell being uniquely addressable through the intersection of a row control line (e.g., a word line) and a column control line (e.g., a bit line), the selection thereof being governed by a row decoder circuit and a column decoder circuit, respectively.

It is often desirable, in the design and fabrication of integrated circuits incorporating such memory arrays, to additionally provide non-memory circuit elements—including, without limitation, test structures, calibration elements, redundancy fuses, reference cells, process-monitoring structures, or configuration elements—within proximity to the memory array. Conventional approaches require the provision of separate, dedicated addressing infrastructure, including additional decoder circuitry and additional control lines, for accessing such non-memory elements independently of the memory array. Such duplicative addressing infrastructure undesirably increases circuit area, layout complexity, and manufacturing cost.

There exists, therefore, a need in the art for a circuit architecture in which non-memory elements may be selectively accessed utilizing the same row and column control lines, and the same associated decoder circuitry, as are utilized for accessing the mask-programmable memory cells, thereby obviating the need for separate addressing infrastructure dedicated solely to said non-memory elements.

---

### SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with the present invention, there is provided an integrated circuit comprising: a first array of mask-programmable memory cells arranged in a plurality of rows and a plurality of columns, each memory cell of said first array being coupled to a respective row control line and a respective column control line selected from a plurality of row control lines and a plurality of column control lines; and a second array comprising a plurality of non-memory elements, each non-memory element of said second array being coupled to at least one row control line and at least one column control line selected from said same plurality of row control lines and said same plurality of column control lines utilized by said first array of memory cells.

In one embodiment, the circuit further comprises a row decoder circuit and a column decoder circuit, each operatively coupled to said plurality of row control lines and said plurality of column control lines, respectively, and configured to selectively activate a designated row control line and a designated column control line in response to an address signal received thereby, such that activation of said designated row control line and said designated column control line effects selection of either a memory cell of said first array or a non-memory element of said second array, depending upon an address range corresponding to said address signal.

In a further embodiment, a decoding circuit is provided for distinguishing between address signals directed to said first array and address signals directed to said second array, such that a single addressing scheme, utilizing a shared plurality of row and column control lines, may be employed to selectively access both said mask-programmable memory cells and said non-memory elements.

It is accordingly an object of the present invention to provide a memory architecture that reduces circuit area and layout complexity by sharing addressing infrastructure between a mask-programmable memory array and an array of non-memory elements.

It is a further object of the present invention to provide such a circuit wherein the non-memory elements may comprise, without limitation, fuse elements, redundancy elements, test elements, or reference elements, without departing from the scope of the present invention.

---

### BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

**FIG. 1** is a schematic block diagram illustrating an integrated circuit in accordance with an embodiment of the present invention, depicting a first array of mask-programmable memory cells and a second array of non-memory elements sharing a common plurality of row and column control lines.

**FIG. 2** is a schematic circuit diagram illustrating a representative mask-programmable memory cell suitable for use in the first array of FIG. 1.

**FIG. 3** is a schematic circuit diagram illustrating a representative non-memory element suitable for use in the second array of FIG. 1.

**FIG. 4** is a flow diagram illustrating a method of addressing the shared row and column control lines to selectively access either a memory cell or a non-memory element.

---

### DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

Referring now to FIG. 1, there is shown an integrated circuit **100** comprising a first array **110** of mask-programmable memory cells **112** arranged in rows **114**₁ through **114**ₙ and columns **116**₁ through **116**ₘ. Each memory cell **112** is disposed at an intersection of a respective row control line **114** and a respective column control line **116**.

The integrated circuit **100** further comprises a second array **120** comprising a plurality of non-memory elements **122**. In accordance with the present invention, each non-memory element **122** of said second array **120** is coupled to at least one of said row control lines **114**₁–**114**ₙ and at least one of said column control lines **116**₁–**116**ₘ, said row and column control lines being the same physical conductive lines utilized to address the memory cells **112** of the first array **110**. Notably, the second array **120** does not comprise mask-programmable memory cells configured to store a bit of data in the conventional sense, but rather comprises circuit elements **122** which may, in various embodiments, be selected from the group consisting of: fuse or anti-fuse elements for redundancy repair; reference or calibration cells for sensing margin adjustment; process-monitoring structures; built-in self-test (BIST) elements; and configuration or trim elements for adjusting operational parameters of the integrated circuit **100**.

A row decoder **130** is coupled to said plurality of row control lines **114**₁–**114**ₙ and is configured to receive a row address signal via address input **132** and, responsive thereto, to selectively activate a designated one of said row control lines. Similarly, a column decoder **140** is coupled to said plurality of column control lines **116**₁–**116**ₘ and is configured to receive a column address signal via address input **142** and, responsive thereto, to selectively activate a designated one of said column control lines.

It shall be understood that, in accordance with the present invention, the row decoder **130** and the column decoder **140** are shared between the first array **110** and the second array **120**, such that no dedicated or duplicative decoder circuitry is required for addressing the non-memory elements **122** independently of the memory cells **112**.

In one embodiment, a discrimination circuit **150** is coupled to receive the address signals provided to said row decoder **130** and said column decoder **140**, and is configured to determine, based upon a predetermined address range or address mapping, whether a given combination of activated row and column control lines corresponds to a memory cell **112** of the first array **110** or a non-memory element **122** of the second array **120**. In a further embodiment, the discrimination circuit **150** comprises a mode-selection input **152** for receiving an external mode-select signal indicative of whether the addressed circuit element is to be treated as a memory cell or a non-memory element for purposes of subsequent signal processing, e.g., by sense amplifier circuitry **160** coupled to said column control lines **116**₁–**116**ₘ.

Referring now to FIG. 2, there is shown a representative mask-programmable memory cell **112**, comprising a select transistor **210** having a gate terminal coupled to a row control line **114**, a source/drain terminal coupled to a column control line **116**, and an opposing source/drain terminal selectively coupled to a reference potential **220** (e.g., ground) via a mask-defined conductive feature **230**, the presence or absence of said conductive feature **230** at the time of fabrication determining the logical state stored by said memory cell **112**.

Referring now to FIG. 3, there is shown a representative non-memory element **122**, comprising a select transistor **310** having a gate terminal coupled to a row control line **114** shared with the memory cell **112** of FIG. 2, and a source/drain terminal coupled to a column control line **116** likewise shared with said memory cell **112**. In the illustrated embodiment, the non-memory element **122** further comprises a fuse element **320** coupled between said select transistor **310** and a reference potential **330**, said fuse element **320** being configured to be selectively blown during a post-fabrication test or trim operation, in contradistinction to the mask-defined conductive feature **230** of the memory cell **112**, which is fixed at the time of fabrication and not subject to post-fabrication modification.

It will be appreciated by persons skilled in the art that the specific configuration of the non-memory element **122** illustrated in FIG. 3 is exemplary only, and that numerous alternative configurations of non-memory elements may be employed within the scope of the present invention, including, without limitation, elements employing capacitive sensing, resistive trimming, or additional transistor-based logic, so long as such elements are addressable via the shared row and column control lines **114**, **116** described herein.

---

a second array of non-memory elements, each non-memory element of said second array being coupled to at least one of said plurality of row control lines and at least one of said plurality of column control lines, said at least one row control line and said at least one column control line being shared with at least one memory cell of said first array.

**2.** The integrated circuit of claim 1, further comprising a row decoder circuit coupled to said plurality of row control lines and a column decoder circuit coupled to said plurality of column control lines, wherein said row decoder circuit and said column decoder circuit are configured to selectively activate said row control lines and said column control lines for accessing both said first array and said second array.

# Technical Description: Semiconductor Memory Device with Mask-Programmable Elements and Dual Control Line Architecture

## Field of the Invention

This disclosure relates to semiconductor memory devices, and more particularly to integrated circuit memory arrays incorporating fabrication-configurable storage elements accessed through a hierarchical control line architecture, wherein a supplementary array of circuit elements provides functional coupling between distinct sets of control conductors.

---

## Background

Semiconductor memory devices commonly employ programmable elements whose logical state is determined not by post-fabrication electrical operations, but by a masking step performed during the semiconductor manufacturing process itself. Such elements—often implemented as selectively formed contacts, vias, implant regions, or metallization patterns—are fixed at the time of manufacture and are not alterable by the end user through electrical programming pulses. This class of device is distinguished from field-programmable or electrically alterable memory technologies (e.g., EEPROM, flash, or antifuse-based OTP arrays) in that the data pattern is embedded lithographically.

A persistent challenge in such architectures is the efficient routing of access and control signals to large arrays of mask-defined elements while preserving layout density, minimizing parasitic loading, and enabling auxiliary circuit functions (such as redundancy evaluation, timing calibration, or reference generation) without duplicating the entire control line infrastructure.

---

## Summary of the Invention

An embodiment of the present invention provides a semiconductor memory device comprising:

**(a) A first array of programmable memory elements**, each element having a state established during a fabrication-step masking operation—such as selective formation or omission of a conductive via, contact, diffusion implant, or interconnect segment—such that the logical value stored by each element is fixed and non-volatile from the time of device manufacture, and is not subject to alteration by subsequent electrical programming.

**(b) A first set of control lines**, disposed in a predetermined conductive layer and extending across the first array in a first direction, each control line of the first set being operatively coupled to a corresponding row, column, or block of the programmable memory elements so as to enable selective access—including read access—to individual elements or groups of elements within the first array. The first set of control lines may comprise word lines, select lines, or address lines coupled to access transistors or pass gates associated with each programmable element.

**(c) A second array of circuit elements**, distinct in structure and/or function from the programmable memory elements of the first array, disposed in a region of the substrate separate from the first array, wherein each circuit element of the second array is electrically coupled to at least one control line of the first set and additionally to at least one control line of a second set of control lines. The second set of control lines may extend in a direction transverse to, parallel with, or interleaved among the first set, and may serve functions including, without limitation:

  - reference or dummy element generation for sensing margin calibration;
  - redundancy substitution and defect remapping;
  - address decoding verification or self-test circuitry;
  - timing skew compensation between rows/columns of the first array.

---

## Detailed Structural Description

### 1. Substrate and Array Formation

The device is fabricated upon a semiconductor substrate (e.g., bulk silicon, silicon-on-insulator, or an equivalent substrate) upon which the first array of programmable elements is formed using standard front-end-of-line (FEOL) and middle-of-line (MOL) processing. Programming of each element's logical state is achieved through a masking operation applied at a specific process layer—commonly a contact or via layer inserted late in the process flow (a so-called "late mask" or "metal-option" programming scheme)—permitting maximal reuse of a common base wafer across multiple data patterns.

### 2. First Set of Control Lines

The first set of control lines is formed in a metallization layer overlying the substrate and is electrically connected to access devices (e.g., MOS transistors) associated with each programmable element. Activation of a given control line couples the corresponding programmable element(s) to a sense amplifier or output buffer via a bit line, enabling determination of the mask-defined logic state. The first set of control lines may be organized in a matrix addressing scheme, with row-select and column-select sublines forming the complete access mechanism for the first array.

### 3. Second Array and Dual Coupling

The second array is positioned at the periphery of, or interspersed within, the first array's layout region. Each circuit element of the second array—implemented, for example, as a dummy cell, fuse-based redundancy latch, reference voltage generator, or comparator stage—receives inputs from a control line of the first set (thereby synchronizing its operation with access cycles of the first array) and from a control line of the second set (which may carry redundancy enable signals, test-mode signals, or trim codes). This dual coupling permits the second array to perform auxiliary operations in temporal and functional coordination with first-array accesses without requiring independent addressing infrastructure.

### 4. Signal Flow

During a read operation:
1. An external or internally generated address activates a corresponding line within the first set of control lines.
2. The activated control line enables access to the target programmable element(s) in the first array, whose mask-defined state is sensed and output.
3. Concurrently, the same (or a logically associated) first-set control line signal propagates to the second array, where it is combined with a second-set control line signal to enable an auxiliary function such as reference comparison or redundancy check.
4. The result of the second array's operation may be used to gate, correct, or qualify the primary output of the first array (e.g., substituting a redundant element's output for a defective mask-programmed element).

---

## Claims (Illustrative Form)

1. A semiconductor memory device comprising: a first array of programmable memory elements, each element having a data state fixed by a masking step performed during fabrication of the device; a first plurality of control lines coupled to the first array to enable selective access to the programmable memory elements; and a second array of circuit elements distinct from the programmable memory elements, each circuit element of the second array coupled to at least one control line of the first plurality and to at least one control line of a second plurality of control lines.

2. The device of claim 1, wherein the programmable memory elements comprise mask-defined via or contact structures selectively formed to represent a binary logic state.

3. The device of claim 1, wherein the second array comprises redundancy elements configured to substitute for defective elements of the first array in response to a signal on the second plurality of control lines.

4. The device of claim 1, wherein the second array comprises reference or dummy elements used for sense amplifier calibration during a read operation of the first array.

5. The device of claim 1, wherein the first plurality of control lines extends in a first direction and the second plurality of control lines extends in a second direction transverse to the first direction.

# PATENT SPECIFICATION EXCERPT

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present disclosure relates generally to semiconductor memory devices, and more particularly to a memory circuit architecture comprising a plurality of processable regions configured for programming via material application, a plurality of first control lines enabling multi-state access to said regions, and a secondary element array disposed to provide electrical bridging between the first control lines and a corresponding plurality of second control lines.

---

## BACKGROUND

[0002] Conventional memory architectures often suffer from limitations in scalability, programming precision, and access latency when multi-state storage is required within a compact circuit footprint. Existing solutions typically rely on discrete programming mechanisms that do not readily accommodate post-fabrication material deposition techniques, nor do they provide efficient bridging structures capable of maintaining signal integrity across control line hierarchies. There exists a need for an improved memory circuit that addresses these deficiencies while supporting flexible programming and multi-state read/write operations.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0003] According to one aspect of the present disclosure, a memory circuit is provided comprising:

(a) a substrate having formed thereon a plurality of processable regions, each processable region being configured to store data corresponding to at least one of a plurality of programmable states, wherein each processable region is programmed by application of a material to a corresponding portion of said processable region;

(b) a plurality of first control lines disposed in electrical communication with the plurality of processable regions, each first control line being configured to enable access to at least one processable region among a plurality of programmable states, such that a given first control line supports multi-state access to its associated processable region or regions; and

(c) a secondary element array disposed between the plurality of first control lines and a plurality of second control lines, the secondary element array comprising a plurality of secondary elements, each secondary element being configured to provide a selective electrical bridge between a respective first control line and a respective second control line, thereby enabling signal propagation and state determination across the first and second control line hierarchies.

[0004] In certain embodiments, the material applied to the processable regions comprises a resistive, conductive, or dielectric material selectively deposited to establish a determinable electrical characteristic corresponding to a desired programmable state.

[0005] In certain embodiments, the secondary element array comprises a plurality of two-terminal or three-terminal switching elements, each configured to selectively couple a first control line to a corresponding second control line responsive to a control signal.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### I. Overview of the Memory Circuit Architecture

[0006] Referring now to the accompanying figures, there is shown generally at reference numeral **100** a memory circuit constructed in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. The memory circuit **100** comprises a substrate **102**, upon or within which is formed an array of processable regions **104₁, 104₂, ... 104ₙ** (collectively, "processable regions **104**"), a plurality of first control lines **106₁, 106₂, ... 106ₘ** (collectively, "first control lines **106**"), a secondary element array **108**, and a plurality of second control lines **110₁, 110₂, ... 110ₖ** (collectively, "second control lines **110**").

[0007] It will be understood by persons skilled in the art that the number of processable regions, first control lines, secondary elements, and second control lines may be varied according to design requirements, and that the specific arrangement depicted herein is illustrative and not limiting.

### II. Processable Regions and Material-Based Programming

[0008] Each processable region **104** is configured to be programmed by application of a material to a designated portion thereof. In one embodiment, the material comprises a chalcogenide compound, a metal oxide, a conductive-bridging material, or another material exhibiting a controllable and stable electrical characteristic—such as resistance, capacitance, or threshold voltage—that varies in a repeatable and detectable manner according to the amount, composition, or spatial distribution of the material applied.

[0009] In an embodiment, the application of material to a processable region **104** is performed using a deposition process selected from the group consisting of: physical vapor deposition, chemical vapor deposition, atomic layer deposition, inkjet-based material deposition, and laser-induced forward transfer. The applied material establishes a programmed state among a plurality of available programmable states, wherein each programmable state corresponds to a distinguishable electrical characteristic detectable during a subsequent read operation.

[0010] In a further embodiment, the plurality of programmable states comprises more than two states, such that each processable region **104** is configured to store multi-bit data. For example, a given processable region **104** may be programmed to any of four, eight, or sixteen discrete states, corresponding to two, three, or four bits of data, respectively, depending upon the granularity of material application and the sensitivity of the associated sensing circuitry.

[0011] It is contemplated that the material application may be performed during an initial manufacturing process, during a subsequent programming operation performed by an end user or programming apparatus, or through a combination thereof, such that the memory circuit **100** may be characterized as one-time programmable, multiple-time programmable, or reprogrammable, according to the reversibility of the material's electrical characteristic.

### III. First Control Lines and Multi-State Access

[0012] Each first control line **106** is disposed in electrical communication with at least one processable region **104**, and is configured to enable access thereto across the plurality of programmable states. In an embodiment, a first control line **106** is coupled to a sense amplifier or comparable state-determination circuit configured to distinguish among the plurality of programmable states based upon a signal received via the first control line **106** during a read operation.

[0013] In one embodiment, the first control lines **106** are arranged in a row-wise configuration relative to the processable regions **104**, such that each first control line **106** is coupled to a plurality of processable regions **104** disposed along a common row of the substrate **102**. In an alternative embodiment, the first control lines **106** are arranged in a column-wise configuration, or in a combination of row-wise and column-wise configurations in conjunction with a corresponding plurality of orthogonal control lines.

[0014] The multi-state access enabled by the first control lines **106** permits a controller circuit (not shown) to apply a plurality of distinct reference voltages, current levels, or timing sequences to a given first control line **106**, thereby resolving the programmable state of an associated processable region **104** with a resolution corresponding to the number of available programmable states.

### IV. Secondary Element Array Bridging First and Second Control Lines

[0015] The secondary element array **108** is disposed structurally and electrically between the plurality of first control lines **106** and the plurality of second control lines **110**. The secondary element array **108** comprises a plurality of secondary elements **108₁, 108₂, ... 108ⱼ**, each secondary element being coupled at a first terminal to a respective first control line **106** and at a second terminal to a respective second control line **110**.

[0016] In an embodiment, each secondary element within the secondary element array **108** comprises a selector device, such as a diode, an ovonic threshold switch, a metal-insulator-transition device, or a transistor, configured to selectively enable or inhibit electrical communication between the coupled first control line **106** and second control line **110** responsive to a control or bias signal.

[0017] In operation, the secondary element array **108** functions to bridge signals originating from or directed to the first control lines **106** such that the second control lines **110** may be employed to perform addressing, sensing, or programming operations upon the processable regions **104** without requiring direct electrical connection between the second control lines **110** and the processable regions **104** themselves. This bridging arrangement advantageously permits a reduction in the number of direct connections required to the processable regions **104**, thereby improving circuit density and reducing parasitic capacitance associated with the memory circuit **100**.

[0018] In a further embodiment, the secondary element array **108** is configured to perform a decoding function, such that a particular combination of signals applied to a subset of the second control lines **110** selectively activates a corresponding subset of the first control lines **106**, thereby enabling addressed access to a target processable region **104** among the plurality of processable regions.

[0019] It is further contemplated that the secondary elements of the array **108** may themselves be configured to store or influence state information, such that the secondary element array **108** contributes an additional layer of functional complexity beyond mere electrical bridging, including but not limited to error correction, redundancy mapping, or state-buffering functions.

### V. Alternative Embodiments

[0020] While the foregoing description has proceeded with reference to a substantially planar arrangement of the processable regions **104**, first control lines **106**, secondary element array **108**, and second control lines **110**, it is contemplated that the memory circuit **100** may alternatively be constructed in a three-dimensional, stacked configuration, wherein multiple layers of processable regions **104** are disposed vertically relative to the substrate **102**, and wherein the first control lines **106**, secondary element array **108**, and second control lines **110** are configured to provide access to processable regions **104** disposed across multiple such layers.

[0021] It is to be understood that the embodiments described herein are illustrative of the principles of the invention and that various modifications may be made by persons skilled in the art without departing from the scope of the invention as defined by the appended claims.

---

## CLAIMS (EXEMPLARY)

**Claim 1.** A memory circuit comprising:
a plurality of processable regions, each processable region configured to be programmed by application of a material thereto so as to establish one of a plurality of programmable states;
a plurality of first control lines in electrical communication with the plurality of processable regions, each first control line configured to enable access to at least one processable region among the plurality of programmable states; and
a secondary element array disposed between the plurality of first control lines and a plurality of second control lines, the secondary element array comprising a plurality of secondary elements each configured to selectively bridge a respective first control line and a respective second control line.

**Claim 2.** The memory circuit of claim 1, wherein the material comprises a chalcogenide compound, a metal oxide, or a conductive-bridging material.

**Claim 3.** The memory circuit of claim 1, wherein each secondary element comprises a selector device selected from the group consisting of a diode, an ovonic threshold switch, and a metal-insulator-transition device.

**Claim 4.** The memory circuit of claim 1, wherein the secondary element array is configured to perform a decoding function to enable addressed access to a target processable region.

**Claim 5.** The memory circuit of claim 1, wherein the plurality of programmable states comprises more than two states, such that each processable region is configured to store multi-bit data.
